items.title: Wendy Oxenhorn — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History
items.q: have my CD player blasting in my head, playing to Muddy Waters, to Little Walter...

ctx.x: Which of course. It’s like, what was I thinking? So it ended tragically. But before it ended, he was making some pasta in the apartment on Duke Ellington Boulevard here... I do want to preface it by saying that he really did take me to hear all these great musicians, and he was my introduction to jazz. I had been a bluesman all my life, I just didn’t know it, but he was my introduction to jazz. One day... He had a harmonica, and among the many things he did, he’s a great, great harmonica player. He had it laying…

Then one day I was in the trains... I always used to hear this great old bluesman. Ted Williams, his name was at the time. He would always call me. This was when I would have a kid in a stroller, and he’d say, “Come on, blues lady; come on, come sing with us.” And I couldn’t sing. Hence, the harmonica. I showed him the harmonica one day, and he came over... This is just the most golden moment. It’s so bluesman. He slapped his leg, and he said, “We are going to make googobs of money.” Hah-hah! Because what he…

items.title: Wendy Oxenhorn interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, January 22, 2026
items.q: I’d have Muddy Waters on, you know in my headphones, and I would just wail

ctx.x: Well here’s the thing. The kind of music that you dance to in ballet can be gorgeous: Sibelius, and Mahler, and there are incredible – Erik Satie. You know there are incredible composers that can move you, and the kind of movement that you make, it’s going to be obviously far different. But there is a great beauty and a great expression in doing something slow and, you know bird-like. You know there’s beauty in the slowness and in, you know “The Swan.” Okay. But Saturday morning on “Soul Train,” like that was it.…

was mending my heart over a heartbreak and it was a musician who one of his instruments was the harmonica. So it was sitting on this table and one day we were listening to “Sugar Blue” and I picked it up and I started just – and he goes, you know, “Baby you got something.” And it was like I got bit by that. I would get on the trains, the express train from 96th Street to 14th Street – well my kids – I was a single parent – while my kids were in school. And I would play between the cars so I wouldn’t disturb…
I’m going to pause for one second. Do you have a movable screen?
